summary: Adversarial re-verification of 9 defect candidates across client.rs, mcp.rs, relay.rs: 8 confirmed at the scout's severity (all cited evidence matched actual code), 1 rejected — the relay session-slot leak is impossible because insert runs synchronously before select! can observe the done notification.

files.description: Client candidates: drain_pending lock-across-send, ticketed_url no timeout, WS max_message_size gap — all confirmed by direct read
MCP candidates: TOCTOU, double-exec retry, orphan children, duplicate spawn — all confirmed by direct read
Relay candidates: slot leak REJECTED (insert is synchronous before select); duplicate client_id confirmed Low
Race window confirmed: ptr_eq recheck and tools.insert are two separate inner lock acquisitions; reload's purge can interleave
drain_pending confirmed holding pending mutex across event_tx.send().await; prompt() takes same lock with no timeout
done-vs-insert race disproven; duplicate-id overwrite without abort confirmed at 415-499

architecture: Verification performed by re-reading src/client.rs (full), src/mcp.rs (full incl. 301-395), src/relay.rs:330-660, plus cross-checks into rmcp-3.3.0 registry sources (service.rs Drop impl 1169-1183, child_process.rs ChildWithCleanup::drop 45-55 and graceful_shutdown 81-92).
report: {"verdicts":[{"id":"drain_pending holds pending mutex across","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Medium","reason":"Verified: drain_pending holds the pending mutex while awaiting event_tx.send for PromptDone; the event channel is capped at 64 and Request/PromptDone sends in handle_frame are blocking. If a consumer stalls (or never calls events()) and the channel fills, a link drop parks Reconnect.run inside drain_pending holding the lock, and prompt() — which takes pending.lock().await with no wait_connected/timeout (client.rs:417-446) — blocks forever. Observable hang fully traced in code.","location_final":"src/client.rs:584-604 (drain_pending), 417-446 (prompt)"},{"id":"ticketed_url uses reqwest::Client::new() with","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Medium","reason":"Verified: ticketed_url builds reqwest::Client::new() with no connect/total timeout and awaits send() on POST /v1/ws_ticket; a daemon or proxy accepting TCP but never answering leaves connect() (and the redial closure, same path) blocked indefinitely. The relay path bounds its handshake at 15s; this path bounds nothing.","location_final":"src/client.rs:352-373"},{"id":"Local WS path lacks the max_message_size","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Low","reason":"Verified: connect()/redial use tokio_tungstenite::connect_async with no WebSocketConfig, while the relay path (relay.rs:343-346, 543-546) caps messages/frames at 4MiB. Inconsistent exposure to unbounded frame buffering; robustness hardening, not a directly exploitable path.","location_final":"src/client.rs:84-91, 469-493 vs src/relay.rs:543-546"},{"id":"Removal race re-inserts a removed server's","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Medium","reason":"Race window verified real: ensure_connected's Arc::ptr_eq still-check (inner.read) and the tools retain+insert (separate inner.write) are two independent lock acquisitions (src/mcp.rs:169-189); reload's removal (slot remove + tools.retain at 74-81) can interleave between them. The subsequent insert resurrects the removed server's tools permanently — call() then fails 'MCP server X not running' (servers map no longer has the slot, failing before any reconnect/drop logic) until the name is re-added. Edge-conditioned (reload racing a dial) but observable misbehavior fully traced.","location_final":"src/mcp.rs:169-189 vs 74-81"},{"id":"Transport-error retry can double-execute side-effectful","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Medium","reason":"Verified: call() retries call_tool once on TransportSend | TransportClosed | UnexpectedResponse (src/mcp.rs:324-343). TransportClosed/UnexpectedResponse can occur after the child processed the request (child death or lost/mismatched response post-processing), so a side-effectful tool runs twice; the in-code comment at 322-323 itself concedes this. UnexpectedResponse means a response arrived — classifying it retryable is wrong on its face.","location_final":"src/mcp.rs:322-343"},{"id":"Orphaned MCP children possible at daemon","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Low","reason":"Verified against rmcp-3.3.0: RunningService::drop only cancels via a DropGuard (service.rs:1169-1183, explicitly warning 'call close() or cancel() before dropping'), and ChildWithCleanup::drop kills via tokio::spawn (child_process.rs:45-55) — spawned tasks dropped during tokio runtime teardown may never execute the kill. src/mcp.rs never calls cancel()/close()/graceful_shutdown anywhere, so daemon shutdown can orphan MCP children. Robustness gap at process exit; not a steady-state defect, Low.","location_final":"src/mcp.rs:77-81, 194, 293, 337 (no close/cancel anywhere)"},{"id":"Concurrent ensure_connected callers both pass","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Low","reason":"Verified: ensure_connected checks conn None under the lock then releases it, clears the backoff window, and dials connect_one with no per-flight guard; conn is installed only at the end (keep-first logic drops losing children). N concurrent tool calls to a dead server spawn N children, N-1 discarded. Wasteful but self-limiting and children are killed at install; Low.","location_final":"src/mcp.rs:129-150, 192-195"},{"id":"Session slot leak: task spawned before","verdict":"rejected","severity_final":"Low","reason":"Leak scenario not reconstructible: sessions.insert runs synchronously in the new-client branch immediately after tokio::spawn, before the select! loop is re-entered — the done task cannot be polled (let alone send its notification) until the loop awaits select!, by which time insert has executed. done-then-insert ordering is therefore impossible; the done handler's remove() always finds the entry. Cited evidence matched the code but the interleaving it posits cannot occur.","location_final":"src/relay.rs:495-506, 515-521"},{"id":"Duplicate client_id overwrites live session","verdict":"confirmed","severity_final":"Low","reason":"Verified: the new-client branch (frame with client id, no data key, disconnect!=true) unconditionally spawns a session and sessions.insert overwrites the existing entry without aborting the stored AbortHandle. A repeat connect for the same id (buggy/hostile relay) leaves the old task running, and its later done notification removes the NEW live session's entry, blinding disconnect/backpressure cleanup for the live session. Requires abnormal relay behavior — DoS-grade only, Low.","location_final":"src/relay.rs:415-499 (unguarded insert at 497-499)"}],"notes":"Contradiction between RelayCrypto candidates: finding 2 (duplicate id) describes exactly the overwrite path that finding 1's leak scenario depended on — since insert-before-select makes the leak impossible, only the duplicate-id overwrite (no abort of old task; old task's later done removes the NEW live entry) is the real bookkeeping defect; both derive from the same unguarded insert, so 8 is rejected and 9 confirmed covers the code path. Also noted: handle_frame's ToEvents path awaits event_tx.send without holding the pending lock (guard released at the remove() statement), so the scout's 'same root cause in handle_frame' claim is half right — the pump can stall on a full channel there, but no deadlock via the pending mutex; drain_pending remains the sole mutex-across-await site. rmcp evidence quotes verified verbatim against registry sources (service.rs:1169-1183, child_process.rs:45-55)."}
